rationale: P5 2014 sold the experiment on sharpening a 3.5 sigma discrepancy with the Standard Model that might point to new physics; the measurement was delivered beyond spec (127 ppb, June 2025) but the WP25 prediction (May 2025) replaced the data-driven hadronic vacuum polarization with lattice QCD after CMD-3 made the e+e- data uncombinable, moving the prediction onto the measurement so that there is no tension at current precision. Surprise: the question was answered, by theory moving rather than experiment, and the answer is no discrepancy.

value: LZ 4.2 t-yr (2024): no WIMP, SI limit 2.2 x 10^-48 cm2 at 40 GeV (90% CL), world-leading above 9 GeV; ADMX excludes DFSZ axions 3.27 to 3.34 ueV and reaches KSVZ 4.54 to 5.41 ueV; SuperCDMS SNOLAB science data from mid-2026, no result yet; LZ 2026 extended-window search: one 248 keV event, 2.6 sigma global
rationale: P5 asked for a broad G2 program with at least an order of magnitude gain in cross-section sensitivity over a 1 GeV to 100 TeV range and discovery reach, 2015 to 2024; LZ delivered far more than an order of magnitude (2.2 x 10^-48 cm2 at 40 GeV, roughly two orders below the 2014-era limits, that comparison not re-verified here) and ADMX reached DFSZ sensitivity in a narrow band, but nothing was found and the low-mass leg (SuperCDMS) has no data yet. Partial: the promised reach was delivered and the WIMP question is answered negatively over it, with no discovery and the program still incomplete at the low-mass end; yes is defensible if the promise is read as sensitivity alone.

rationale: P5 asked for small short-baseline experiments that conclusively address the sterile neutrino hints in 2015 to 2020; MicroBooNE ruled out the electron interpretation of the MiniBooNE excess and excluded part of the 3+1 space, ICARUS found no muon neutrino disappearance but is systematics limited, and the decisive two-detector SBND plus ICARUS analysis has not been published as of 2026-10. Partial: the anomaly is much narrowed but not conclusively resolved, and the conclusive test is about six years past the P5 window.

Yes: the core question was answered, at reduced scope (no re-acceleration or sustained cooling), and the answer came despite, not because of, the P5 recommendation.
